functions.get_item(sku: str): returns dict {sku: str, name: str, price: float in dollars (e.g. 12.5 means 12.50 dollars), category: str} or None if sku is unknown
functions.get_customer(customer_id: str): returns dict {id: str, name: str, discount: float as fraction (0.10 means 10 percent), region: str (uppercase US state code, e.g. TX)} or None if id is unknown

value.notes: Lookups are exact-match and case-sensitive. Returned dicts are fresh copies. pricing.py does not apply discounts or tax; callers do.

why: Defines the pricing to invoice/tax interface. Prices are price_cents converted to dollars; discount_pct converted to fraction per team standard; region is needed by tax.py to pick a tax rule.

value: integer cents for all money amounts (1250 = $12.50); tax results returned as integer cents
why: Team coding standard: money as integer cents. Also avoids float drift.

value: percent numbers: 10 means 10%, 8.25 means 8.25%; discount_pct and tax_pct use this form
why: Team coding standard: percentages are percent numbers.

value: tax.compute_tax(region, lines, discount_pct=0) -> int cents. region: customer region code string, or null for an unknown customer. lines: list of (category, amount_cents) pairs, one per order line. discount_pct: customer discount in percent numbers. Raises KeyError if region is a non-null string not in rates.csv. Also tax.tax_rate(region) -> percent number; None -> 0; unknown string -> KeyError.
why: agent3 calls compute_tax per order; agent1 supplies region from the customer record and line amounts/categories. A line is taxable if its category is not in exempt_categories.csv.

value: unknown customer (region null) pays 0 tax, per RULES.md; this is the only null case and does not raise KeyError. Computation is exact (no intermediate rounding); only the final tax is rounded to the cent, ROUND_HALF_UP.
why: RULES.md says an unknown customer pays 0%, which conflicts with the KeyError standard, so I reconcile it: the caller signals an unknown customer with null; an unknown region string raises KeyError.

value.rounding: Decimal.quantize(Decimal("0.01"), ROUND_HALF_UP) for every money amount that is stored or shown

why: Team coding standard; the rounding mode is needed so discount and tax agree on cents.

value.get_unit_price(sku): returns Decimal unit price; Decimal("0") if sku unknown
value.has_sku(sku): returns bool; used to tell unknown SKUs from a known SKU priced at 0
value.get_customer_discount(customer_id): returns Decimal multiplier of the price kept (10% off -> Decimal("0.90")); unknown customer -> Decimal("1")

why: render_invoice needs to tell unknown SKUs apart; discount uses the multiplier convention.

value.get_tax(customer_id, taxable_lines): taxable_lines = list of (sku, net_amount) where net_amount = line amount * discount multiplier, NOT rounded; returns (tax_amount, tax_multiplier)
value.tax_amount: Decimal, rounded to cent HALF_UP; tax.py decides which skus are taxable (example: only sku A is taxable, 22.50 * 0.0825 = 1.86)
value.tax_multiplier: Decimal, 1.0825 for 8.25%; Decimal("1") when the customer has no tax (unknown customer -> tax_amount Decimal("0"), multiplier 1)

why: Tax depends on per-SKU taxability and on the discounted amounts, so tax.py must receive SKUs and net line amounts. The discount itself is computed in invoice.py.
Superseded: agent2 proposed integer cents and percent numbers (money-units, percent-units). Resubmitting pricing_api in those units, which match the raw data columns price_cents and discount_pct.
